sections.brief: Open the stage with the country Herzl's program was aimed at, as it stood around 1896–1914: Ottoman provinces with no border (the 1872 Mutasarrifate of Jerusalem with Jaffa, Hebron, Beersheba and Gaza; the Nablus and Acre sanjaks), the millet system and its costs (me_s01), imperial rule rather than settlement (tk_s01), and the Old Yishuv in the four holy cities living on the halukka (about 7,000 Jews in 1800, about 27,000 in 1880). Present the population dispute from both sides with a fig-compare table: Ottoman 1914–15 census 722,000 with 39,000 Jews (Ottoman subjects only) against Bachi's 689,000 with 94,000 Jews, McCarthy's ~60,000 and the long-standard 85,000, and say why the counts differ. Mention in a sentence that Jews had lived in Iraq since 586 BCE (irq_e01) and link forward to the Mizrahi story rather than telling it; link back to rd0's ot_s01 for the 1858 Land Code. Map: me_layers.

Basel, 29–31 August 1897: Herzl as convener and his diary prediction; the Basel Program quoted from the primary text (aim and four means; 'Heimstätte', not 'state'; the rechtlich/öffentlich-rechtlich change); the founding of the Zionist Organization. Tell the Munich refusal precisely (the 5 June notice, the congregation's letter, the 6 July Protestrabbiner declaration with its five signatories and its quoted words, Hermann Adler's agreement), then the Bund, Orthodox anti-Zionism, Ahad Ha'am and Edmond de Rothschild's opposition (link back to rd0's bc_s04; keep the two Rothschilds distinct). Present two disputes: delegate numbers (208 from 17 countries / about 200 / 14 states) and whether Dreyfus was Herzl's catalyst (Beller notes Dreyfus is absent from the 1895 diary). Note the 'Nile to Euphrates' misattribution as the scene gives it. Figure: fig-compare of the Basel Program's four means against what each later produced (JCT, JNF, federations, charter diplomacy). Map: state_build.

How the organization worked, 1897–1917: the shekel, the 1899 constitution's 7-member Smaller and 37-member Larger Actions Committees, yearly then biennial Congresses, the national federations (American 1898, English 1899). Walk the Congresses 1898–1913 in one fig-time (JCT groundwork 1898; funds only for Palestine or Syria 1899; London 1900; JNF and the Democratic Faction 1901; East Africa 1903; rejection and Wolffsohn 1905; practical vs political and Ruppin's Palestine branch 1907; Hamburg 1909; first Hebrew session and Otto Warburg 1911; Hebrew University 1913). Close with wartime neutrality, Weizmann and Sokolow in London, the May 1917 anti-Zionist statement of the Board of Deputies and Anglo-Jewish Association, and why the letter went to Lord Rothschild; link to [scene:s06] for the Declaration itself rather than retelling it. Figure: fig-tree of the organization's structure.

Herzl's search for a charter from any great power, in order: the Kaiser (three meetings in 1898 via William Hechler), the Sultan (17 May 1901; debt relief offered; the 'not even a foot of land' message from Herzl's diary, tk_s02), the El-Arish plan and Cromer's veto over Nile water (1902–03), Plehve after Kishinev (August 1903) and the Russian Zionists' backlash, and Pius X's refusal in January 1904 (tell only the 1904 audience from vat_s01 and bc_s08; link forward for 1948–1993). Explain the Ottoman restrictions on Jewish immigration and land purchase from the 1880s and how they were evaded (tk_s02), linking to s04j for the legal detail. Kishinev itself is told in s04e; mention it and link. Figures: fig-time of the approaches 1898–1904; fig-compare of what Herzl offered each power and what each answered. Map: turkey_arc.

Herzl and the existing population, 1895–1905, told in order: the June 1895 diary passage on 'spiriting' the penniless population across the border, with the dispute stated from both sides (Arieli reads it as an early transfer idea; Beller, on Penslar, says it concerned South America and that Herzl preferred peaceful means); Yusuf Diya al-Khalidi's letter of 1 March 1899 via Zadoc Kahn and Herzl's reply of 19 March, with Rashid Khalidi's reading and Herzl's own words; Altneuland (1902) and Reschid Bey; Zangwill's 1905 statement. Tell from sq_s05 only the origin of 'a land without a people' (Keith 1843, Shaftesbury 1853, Zangwill 1901) and link forward for the later slogans. Point back to Ahad Ha'am's 1891 warning in s04. Figure: fig-compare of al-Khalidi's letter and Herzl's reply, point by point.

The Jewish Colonial Trust: decided 1898, incorporated in London 20 March 1899, £2,000,000 authorized in £1 shares on installments of up to 55–80 payments; Herzl's first 1,000 shares; about 250,000 shares sold (~£250,000, 12.5% of target); co-founders Wolffsohn and Kahn; the founders'-shares control structure (point to s04j's funding pipeline rather than repeating it); the Anglo-Palestine Company spun off on 27 February 1902. Discuss the numbers in the panels money_1948:The Streams:0 and global_funding:Year by Year:0 (the JCT row, ~$47M in today's dollars, and its method). Figures: fig-money for the JCT chain; fig-stats of the target, the raise and the share price. Map: money_1948.

The Jewish National Fund, 29 December 1901: Schapira's 1897 proposal, the repeated deferrals and Herzl forcing the vote, the founding resolution's wording, Kremenetzky in Vienna, Kleinman's blue box (c.1904; about a million by the interwar years), Goldberg's 200-dunam first parcel east of Hadera (1903), and the leased-never-sold rule. Carry the land series through to 1947–48 (22,363 / ~89,500 acres and 108 communities / 516,000 / ~936,000 dunams; ~7% of ~26 million dunams) and discuss panel money_1948:Land & People:0. pm_s01 only repeats these figures: link it, do not retell. Figure: fig-time of the land totals.

Two tracks, 1902–1903: the Anglo-Palestine Company (founded 27 February 1902, ~£50,000, Wolffsohn chair, Levontin manager, Jaffa branch 1903, branches to 1914, later Bank Leumi) and its loan to Ahuzat Bayit; then Kishinev (6–7 April 1903: 49 killed, 500+ injured, the Bessarabets incitement, the role attributed to Plehve, the world reaction) and the scale of emigration it fed (2.5 million left Eastern Europe 1881–1914, about 2 million to the US). Then Chamberlain's Guas Ngishu offer, Herzl's 'Zion this certainly is not' framing, the vote of 295–178 with 98 abstentions, and the Russian walkout. Name the source conflict on the vote (one other scene gives 295–177). Figure: fig-stats for Kishinev and emigration.

The Seventh Congress (Basel, 27 July–2 August 1905) rejects East Africa and elects Wolffsohn; Zangwill leads 28 delegates out and founds the ITO; its search (Canada, Australia, Mesopotamia, Cyrenaica, Angola, Galveston), Zangwill's court case against the JCT, his return before his 1921 death and the ITO's end around 1925; Otto Warburg's own pro-Uganda past. State plainly what 'confirmed by elimination' does and does not show. Figure: fig-time 1903–1925 of the territorial question.

The Uganda counterfactual, written and labeled as a reading, not a finding: Genesis 15:18, Herzl's 1896 Argentina/Palestine passage ('We shall take what is given us' from gia_src_s01), Scofield's sequence (link to s05), the IS-RA-EL lens (clearly labeled interpretation), and what is portable (finance, land offices) versus what is not (the scriptural layer). From gia_src_s01 add the Greater Israel argument and the 'territorial vs. Zion' split, and give the other side fairly: the record shows Russian delegates' attachment to Zion, and the scene itself says counterfactuals cannot be documented. Figure: fig-compare of what survives a move and what does not.

Jewish positions for and against, 1885–1914, as plurality rather than consensus: Reform's Pittsburgh Platform (1885) and the CCAR's 1897 resolution and Wise; the Democratic Faction and the 1901 turn to culture; Mizrachi (Vilna, 4–5 March 1902; Reines; 210 branches; the 1911 walkout); Frankfurt Orthodox opposition (Breuer 1903); Agudat Israel (Kattowitz, May 1912; from df_s13 tell only its 1912 founding and link forward for later material); Germany's Antizionistisches Komitee (1912–14, its numbers); the League of British Jews (November 1917, link to [scene:s06]). Figure: fig-compare of the main currents: who, when, on Palestine, on a state.

The Second Aliyah, 1904–1914: numbers with the 35,000/40,000 dispute and the half who left; Ben-Gurion's arrival (state the 1906/1907 source conflict); Hebrew labor and its limits; Bar-Giora (1907) and Hashomer (1909–1920); Kinneret farm, Degania (state the 1909/1910 dispute), Merhavia, the women's farm; the Hebrew Gymnasium and Tel Aviv's lots (Passover 1909, 60 families); the ICA's management of Rothschild's colonies (1899/1900 conflict). Tell the Yemenite story in full: 1881–82, Kfar Hashiloach 1884, Yavne'eli's 1911–12 mission, the numbers, and the Kinneret group (link forward for its 1930 removal). Present the historians' dispute fairly: Shafir's land-and-labor reading against Shapira's. Figure: fig-time 1904–1914; fig-stats of the numbers.

The Palestine Office, Jaffa, 1908: Wolffsohn sends Ruppin in 1907; the office's functions; the Palestine Land Development Company with Otto Warburg (dated 1908 or 1909 across sources; say so), about 50,000 dunams by 1914; the agents Hankin, Ruppin and Thon; the line to the Jewish Agency of 1929. Ruppin's racial views belong in s04j; mention and link. Figure: fig-flow from fundraising (JCT/JNF) to purchase (PLDC) to settlement; discuss panel money_1948:The Machine:0.

The Scofield Reference Bible (Oxford University Press, 1909): Scofield's documented biography, Darby's prior framework, the notes-on-the-page mechanism, the 1917 second edition, the Untermyer association (state it as Canfield documents it, not as causation), OUP's governance by its Delegates, the theological dispute the scene raises (keep the IS-RA-EL passage clearly labeled as interpretation), and the intra-Christian critique (Kairos 2009). The chain to Dallas Seminary, Lindsey, Falwell, Left Behind and CUFI belongs to later volumes: summarize it briefly, give the Pew and constituency figures exactly as the scene does with their sources, and link forward (bwm_src_s15 only as a link). Link back to rd0's bc_s05 for the restorationists before Scofield. Map: christian_zionism.

The land mechanism, centered on its pre-1917 beginnings and carried to its documented results: the Sursock chain (1872 Ottoman sale; the al-Fula/Merhavia purchase of February 1910, 9,500 dunams, the Nazareth governor Shukri al-Asali's opposition and his 1916 execution; the 1920–25 main sales); mulk and miri and why tenants held no title; the Ottoman restrictions of 1881–83 and 1892, their evasion (including the Lowenstein case) and the ~418,000 dunams held by 1918; JNF, PLDC and PICA; the funding pipeline and founders' shares; Ruppin's office and his documented racial views; Antébi and the Old Yishuv; then forward in brief to Wadi al-Hawarith (1929–33), the five tenant laws and 1938. Present the dispute: Ruppin's memoir (willing sellers, Hankin trusted) against the Arab officials' and tenants' record. Figures: fig-money of the purchase chain; fig-time from 1872 to 1938; discuss panel money_1948:Land & People:1.

The Palestinian public sphere before 1914: Azouri's 1905 prediction; Najib Nassar's campaign from 1905, al-Karmil (Haifa, 1908), its closure in 1909, his trial and acquittal, his 1911 book and 1914 appeal; Filastin (Jaffa, 15 January 1911, Issa and Yousef El-Issa), its turn from ambivalence to hostility by 1914, copies to every village of the Jaffa district, its run to 7 April 1948 and 6,692 preserved issues; Ruhi al-Khalidi and Sa'id al-Husayni in the Ottoman parliament (1911); the Paris Arab Congress of June 1913 and its silence on Zionism. Answer the 'invented later' claim from the record. Figure: fig-time of Arab press and political responses, 1905–1914.

The American machine, 1912–1918: Szold and Hadassah (24 February 1912; 38–122 founders; nurses in 1913; Youth Aliyah later), Brandeis's 1914 turn via de Haas, the Wilson channel and the Blackstone Memorial (1916), Goldmann's assessment given as one historian's view, the motive dispute stated as open, the ZOA's 1918 merger and 147,551 members, and the 1921 Cleveland split (link forward). Link to [scene:s06] for Brandeis's part in the Declaration rather than retelling the drafting. Figure: fig-tree of the American organizations in 1918; discuss panel prestate_funding:The Build:0 (its 1912–18 row).

The Federal Reserve, 1913, told as one section: first what it is (the hybrid of twelve member-owned Reserve Banks and a Senate-confirmed Board), the panics roughly every fifteen years and 1907's Morgan rescue, Jekyll Island (November 1910) with its six named participants and the stated reason for secrecy, and how Congress cut private control before the Act of 23 December 1913; then why this book draws no line from it to Zionist finance: Paul Warburg's documented role, Jacob Schiff's and Felix Warburg's on-record non-Zionism, and the claim's origin in Eustace Mullins's 1950s tract. Use plain procedural language throughout, never conspiracy-coded words. Figure: fig-tree of the Fed's structure; fig-compare of the Aldrich Plan and the 1913 Act. Map: fed_1913.

Palestine at war, 1914–1917, for all its people: the December 1914 expulsion of Russian-citizen Jews from Jaffa and the refugees in Alexandria; the 1915 Ottomanization order; the locusts of March–October 1915 (Foster's harvest losses; the locust-egg quota) and the famine in Greater Syria with both mortality figures; the hangings of Arab nationalists, including al-Asali (6 May 1916; note that the AUB exhibit dates the Damascus and Beirut executions to 1915); the Jaffa and Tel Aviv evacuation (order 28 March, deportation 6 April 1917), the range of numbers, the unequal return, about 1,500 deaths; and the dispute over how far the Jewish population fell. Do not retell the wartime promises: link to [scene:s06] and say Stage Two tells them. Figure: fig-time 1914–1917; fig-stats with the disputed ranges.

Services rendered to Britain, 1915–1918: NILI (about 40 members, the Aaronsohns and Feinberg, the British vessel, Aaronsohn's 1916 briefings of Sykes and Ormsby-Gore, the October 1917 collapse and Sarah Aaronsohn's death), the Zion Mule Corps at Gallipoli (737 volunteers, many of them refugees from rd1_wwi), and the Jewish Legion (38th–42nd Royal Fusiliers, the Nova Scotia battalion with Ben-Gurion, Weizmann's and Jabotinsky's support against the British Zionist leadership's opposition). State what the record shows about whether these services shaped the Declaration and what it does not; link to [scene:s06] for the Declaration and its three-promise context (me_s04, or_s01, me_s03 are told in Stage Two). Figure: fig-time 1915–1918.

Closing synthesis: the five dates (1896, 1903–05, 1917, 1920, 1922) against 1933 and the Holocaust, with Biltmore (1942) as acceleration not origin, stated as the scene states it and without minimizing the Holocaust. Then the architecture as it stood in 1917: a Congress and executive, federations in the US and Britain, a bank and a Jaffa branch, a land fund with its land, a Palestine Office and land company, a labor movement and guards, an American constituency, and, against them, an Ottoman state, Arab press and deputies, and Jewish dissent. Discuss panels year_ledger:Part 1:0 and prestate_funding:The Build:0. Figures: one synthesis fig-tree of the 1917 structure; a fig-time of the five dates. Link forward to [scene:s06]. Map: state_build.
